0.question: How long does it take to build a landing page?

1.question: Can I update the content myself after launch?
1.answer: Yes. Your page can ship with a headless CMS like Sanity or Contentful so you can edit text, images, and sections without touching code. Alternatively, you get the Git repository handed off for developer-managed updates.

landingPages.approach: Everything starts with your conversion goal and works backward. Every layout decision, copy block, and interaction is designed to move visitors toward one clear action. wordpressMigration.title: WordPress → Next.js Migration
wordpressMigration.tagline: From slow to instant. In 1-2 weeks.
wordpressMigration.description: Your WordPress site, migrated to a fast Next.js stack: AI-assisted, scoped around your content and SEO risk, with a 90+ PageSpeed target. The migration replaces plugin maintenance with a cleaner application architecture.

features.1: Next.js static generation with a 90+ PageSpeed target

deliverables.1: Next.js static generation with a 90+ PageSpeed target

0.heading: Your WordPress site is costing you every day
0.description: Plugin subscriptions, managed hosting, developer bills for routine updates. Add it up and your WordPress site costs more per year than rebuilding it once in Next.js.

1.heading: Slow speed is killing your conversions
1.description: Run your own site through PageSpeed Insights. If you're on WordPress, you already know what the score looks like. Every second of load time costs you visitors who will never come back.

2.heading: Security patches are a full-time job
2.description: Another week, another plugin update. Another security advisory you're not sure applies to you. Static sites built in Next.js don't have a plugin layer to exploit.

0.question: Will I lose my SEO rankings during migration?
0.answer: Migration risk is reduced with URL mapping, 301 redirects, metadata preservation, sitemap review, performance checks, and post-launch monitoring. Rankings can still move during a migration, so the cutover is planned carefully.

1.question: Can I keep my WordPress content workflow?
1.answer: Yes. Your site can connect to a headless CMS that feels similar to WordPress but serves content through Next.js. You keep the familiar editing experience with dramatically better frontend performance.

2.question: How long does a typical migration take?
2.answer: Simple brochure sites: 2-3 weeks. E-commerce or complex sites with custom plugins: 4-6 weeks. Both sites run in parallel during migration, with the cutover planned to minimize downtime.

3.question: What happens to my WordPress plugins?
3.answer: Each plugin is audited and replaced with a modern equivalent. Contact forms become API routes, SEO plugins become built-in Next.js metadata, analytics move to PostHog or GA4, and caching becomes unnecessary with static generation.

4.question: What does the first week of a migration actually look like?
4.answer: Day one is a full audit of your existing site: pages, plugins, SEO structure, and hosting costs. By day three, you see a working prototype in Next.js with your content and branding. The rest of week one is refinement, redirect mapping, and performance benchmarking. You're involved at every step, but you don't have to manage the process.

wordpressMigration.approach: A full audit of your WordPress site comes first: every page, plugin, redirect, and SEO signal. Then the site is rebuilt in Next.js with static generation, preserving your content and branding while reducing the maintenance overhead. Redirects are mapped, metadata is preserved, and rankings are monitored after launch.
wordpressMigration.outcome: A site that loads quickly, targets 90+ on PageSpeed, and requires much less maintenance. No more constant plugin updates, recurring security patches, or hosting fees that creep up every year. Your content stays exactly where Google expects it.

results.webVitalsSubtitle: These metrics directly affect how users experience your site and how Google ranks it.

vitalExplanations.FCP: First Contentful Paint: how quickly visitors see the first content. A slow FCP means users stare at a blank screen and are more likely to leave before your page even appears.
vitalExplanations.LCP: Largest Contentful Paint: when the main content becomes visible. If this takes longer than 2.5 seconds, roughly half of mobile visitors will leave before seeing your message.
vitalExplanations.TBT: Total Blocking Time: how long the page is unresponsive to clicks and taps. High blocking time means frustrated users who tap buttons and nothing happens.
vitalExplanations.CLS: Cumulative Layout Shift: how much the page layout jumps around while loading. Shifting content causes users to accidentally click the wrong thing, damaging trust.
vitalExplanations.SI: Speed Index: how quickly the visible area of your page is populated. A slow Speed Index means your site feels sluggish even if it eventually loads.
vitalExplanations.default: This metric affects how users perceive your site's speed and responsiveness.

intro.tagline: Founder of webvise. AI-native product engineer.
intro.description: Engineer at the intersection of design, full-stack development, and AI automation.

paragraphs.0: I studied visual communication and design in Berlin and spent my early career in agencies, building websites and campaigns that connected creative work with business outcomes. That foundation in design thinking still shapes every project at webvise.
paragraphs.1: In 2017, I took on the CEO role at a recruiting technology company, where I raised funding and led the team in designing and implementing the core matching algorithm. Running a startup taught me what it takes to ship fast under real constraints.
paragraphs.2: After that chapter, I founded webvise. What started as a design studio evolved into a full-stack practice delivering web applications, branding, and AI automation for businesses across the globe.
paragraphs.3: Before webvise became the current studio, I led product and engineering work across startups and client teams. That shaped the delivery model I use today: scoped systems, fast shipping, and direct ownership.
paragraphs.4: My current work focuses on production AI engineering: LLM-assisted internal tools, automation pipelines, and software systems that people use in real operations. That practical experience shapes how webvise approaches AI projects: start with the workflow, define the controls, ship a system the team can run.
paragraphs.5: In 2025, I collaborated with a team spanning Bangkok and Berlin to build an AI-powered game engine extension, further deepening my applied AI expertise. Today, webvise combines everything I have built across design, engineering, product, and AI into a practice that ships production software in weeks.

0.description: Design, development, and AI automation for businesses across the globe. From branding and landing pages to full-stack applications with AI-powered chatbots, multilingual content systems, and workflow automation. Every project ships through an AI-first development workflow using Claude Code and self-hosted agent orchestration.

1.description: Builds LLM-assisted internal tools, automation pipelines, and AI integrations in production environments. This practical engineering work informs how webvise designs AI-assisted workflows for clients.

2.description: Shipped B2B product interfaces in close collaboration with designers and operators, building the frontend engineering discipline that supports webvise's delivery model.

3.description: Built and shipped a product from concept to public launch with a distributed international team. Experience in rapid technical execution, product packaging, and cross-time-zone delivery.

4.description: Raised funding and led delivery of a recruiting platform, including the core matching logic. Startup operating experience that shapes how webvise scopes client projects: business first, ship quickly, iterate from real use.

5.description: Designed websites and campaigns, managed digital advertising, content strategy, and social media for consulting clients. Five years of hands-on marketing and project management experience that now informs webvise's data-driven approach to SEO, conversion optimization, and AI-powered content workflows.

6.role: B.A. Graphic Design and Visual Communication
6.description: Studied typography, corporate design, illustration, photography, motion design, editorial design, and web/app design. The foundation in visual communication that shapes every webvise project.

internalTools.title: Internal tools and dashboards
internalTools.description: Custom dashboards and admin tools for teams that need one reliable place to manage data, workflows, users, and operations.

detail.metaDescription: Custom internal tools, admin dashboards, reporting interfaces, and operational software, designed and built by one accountable engineer.
detail.heroTitle: Internal tools and dashboards for teams that need one reliable place to work.
detail.heroSubtitle: webvise designs and builds internal CRMs, admin panels, reporting tools, data tables, workflow status views, and team operations software around the way your business actually runs.
detail.scope: Workflow, data model, roles, dashboards, admin actions, integrations, and deployment.
detail.timeline: Focused builds can ship quickly. Larger tools are planned in phases with a clear scope before implementation.
detail.approach: The work starts by mapping the operational workflow, the people involved, the decisions they make, and the systems that already hold the data. From there, the interface, backend logic, permissions, and integration layer are designed as one product.
detail.outcome: Your team gets a practical operations system that replaces spreadsheets, scattered admin screens, and manual handoffs with one reliable application.
capabilities: Role-based admin dashboards for teams, managers, and operators.
Editable data tables with filtering, search, bulk actions, and audit-friendly changes.
Internal CRM views for leads, customers, members, partners, or suppliers.
Reporting dashboards that combine operational data into useful decisions.
Workflow status views for approvals, assignments, queues, and handoffs.
Integrations with forms, CRMs, databases, email, analytics, and existing tools.
modules: Login, permissions, and team roles.
Dashboard overview with the metrics that matter.
CRUD interfaces for operational data.
Search, filters, sorting, exports, and activity history.
Notifications, assignment flows, and approval steps.
Deployment, monitoring, and post-launch improvement support.
outcomes: Less operational work hidden in spreadsheets.
Clearer ownership of tasks, records, and next steps.
Faster reporting without manual copy-paste work.
A system that can grow as the workflow matures.

faq.question: Can you replace our spreadsheets or Airtable base?
faq.answer: Yes. Spreadsheet-driven operations can become a custom application with roles, validation, workflows, reporting, and integrations while preserving the useful parts of your current process.

faq.question: Can this connect to our existing tools?
faq.answer: Usually yes. Common integrations include CRMs, forms, email platforms, analytics tools, databases, payment systems, and internal APIs. Integration effort is scoped before the build starts.

faq.question: Do you also design the UX?
faq.answer: Yes. The same engineer works on workflow understanding, UX structure, backend logic, and deployment, so the interface is designed around real operational decisions.

aiWorkflows.title: AI-assisted workflow automation
aiWorkflows.description: Human-in-the-loop AI workflows for repeated work like document processing, lead research, support triage, reporting, and internal handoffs.

detail.metaDescription: Human-in-the-loop AI automation for document processing, triage, approvals, reporting, content operations, and internal handoffs.
detail.heroTitle: AI-assisted workflow automation that keeps humans in control.
detail.heroSubtitle: webvise builds practical AI workflows for repeated operational work: document extraction, lead research, support triage, approval queues, reporting drafts, content operations, RAG systems, and custom assistants.
detail.scope: Workflow design, AI task boundaries, human review, data handling, integrations, safety checks, and monitoring.
detail.timeline: Scoped around the workflow risk. Prototype first when model behavior needs validation.
detail.approach: The work starts by separating what AI should draft, classify, extract, or suggest from what a person should approve. The review loop, data flow, prompts, model calls, fallbacks, and operational interface are then designed around that boundary.
detail.outcome: Your team gets a faster workflow without handing important judgement to a black box. AI handles repetitive steps, people stay responsible for decisions.
capabilities: Document extraction and structured data capture from messy inputs.
Support, lead, or request triage with confidence-aware routing.
Approval queues where AI drafts and humans review before action.
Reporting drafts, summaries, and internal handoff notes.
RAG systems and custom assistants grounded in your own knowledge base.
Monitoring, logging, and fallback paths for production use.
modules: Input capture from forms, inboxes, documents, or databases.
Prompt, model, and tool orchestration for the specific task.
Human review interface with approve, edit, reject, and escalate actions.
Structured outputs saved back into the system of record.
Evaluation checks, confidence signals, and error handling.
Analytics for throughput, accuracy, and manual override patterns.
outcomes: Less repetitive manual processing.
Shorter response and handoff times.
More consistent triage, extraction, and reporting.
AI usage that is visible, reviewable, and operationally useful.

faq.question: Do you build fully autonomous AI agents?
faq.answer: Only when the risk profile supports it. Most business workflows work better with human-in-the-loop automation, where AI drafts, extracts, classifies, or recommends and a person approves important actions.

faq.question: Can you use our documents or internal knowledge?
faq.answer: Yes. Retrieval-based workflows and assistants that use your approved knowledge sources can be built. Access control, data handling, and update processes are scoped up front.

faq.question: How do you avoid hypey AI experiments?
faq.answer: The project starts from the workflow and business outcome. If AI does not improve speed, quality, consistency, or cost in a measurable way, it should not be the centre of the build.

detail.timeline: Planned in phases when multiple user roles, integrations, or workflows are involved.
detail.approach: The work starts by defining who uses the portal, what they should see, what they can change, and what the business needs to manage behind the scenes. The portal is then designed as both a user-facing product and an internal operations tool.

Clearer status visibility for users and internal teams.

faq.question: Can you build portals with different user roles?
faq.answer: Yes. Roles and permissions are a core part of portal scope, including what each user type can view, submit, edit, approve, or manage.

faq.question: Can users upload files and track status?
faq.answer: Yes. File uploads, review states, status timelines, notifications, and admin review screens can all be part of the build.

faq.question: Can the portal connect to our CRM or backend?
faq.answer: Yes. Integrations are scoped around the systems you already use, such as CRM, payments, databases, email tools, analytics, and internal APIs.

faq.question: Can this support multiple event types or locations?
faq.answer: Yes. Event types, locations, sessions, capacity rules, and registration flows can be modelled around your actual program structure.

faq.question: Can it send reminders and follow-ups?

faq.question: Can it include payments or CRM sync?
faq.answer: Yes. Payments, CRM sync, email marketing, calendars, analytics, and exports can be scoped as integrations.

faq.question: Can you preserve SEO during a migration?
faq.answer: Yes. URL structure, redirects, metadata, content hierarchy, performance, and technical SEO are part of the migration scope when an existing site is being replaced.

faq.question: Is this only for WordPress sites?
faq.answer: No. It also applies to static websites, Webflow-style sites, or older custom sites that need to become faster, more integrated, or more application-like.

faq.question: Can the upgraded site include dashboards or AI features?
faq.answer: Yes. The upgrade can include forms, dashboards, CRM sync, AI assistants, automation workflows, and admin tools depending on the business need.

The loop stays tight here: you work directly with Sebastian, the engineer responsible for understanding the workflow, designing the system, building the application, and shipping it to production.
